questions.question: For LT11 or Letter 1058, what does the IRS say to do if I cannot pay the full overdue balance?
expected_answer_facts: Paying part of the balance now reduces future interest and applicable penalties.
A taxpayer who is current on required filings may request an installment agreement.
A balance below $50,000 may qualify for the online installment-agreement process.
A taxpayer unable to pay should contact the telephone number on the notice or letter.

response.answer:
IRS guidance says: If you can’t pay the full amount, pay what you can now; payments will reduce the amount of interest and applicable penalties added to the remaining balance in the future. IRS guidance says: If you’re current on your tax filings, you can request an [installment agreement](https://www.irs.gov/payments/payment-plans-installment-agreements) to pay the remaining balance on your account over time.

Note: If you owe less than $50,000, you may be able to set up an installment agreement using the [Online Payment Agreement tool](https://www.irs.gov/payments/online-payment-agreement-application), which is the fastest way to get an installment agreement approved. IRS guidance says: If you can’t apply online, call us at the number on your notice or letter, or mail in an [installment agreement request PDF](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f9465--dft.pdf). IRS guidance says: If you’re unable to pay the balance due, contact the telephone number listed on the notice or letter.

questions.question: The IRS says it still hasn't heard from me and calls this my second reminder about an unpaid balance. What stage is this, and what could happen if I keep ignoring it?
expected_answer_facts: The unpaid balance remains and the IRS has not received a payment or response.

The balance should be paid by the notice's due date to avoid additional penalties and interest.
Continued nonresponse may lead to a Notice of Federal Tax Lien.

response.answer: IRS guidance says: This notice is your second reminder that you still owe a balance on one of your tax accounts. You received this notice because we haven’t received your payment or a response to previous notice(s) requesting you pay this balance. IRS guidance says: If you don't pay the amount due, make payment arrangements, or contact us at the toll-free number on your notice, we may file a Notice of Federal Tax Lien if we haven't already done so. IRS guidance says: A tax lien is a public notice to your creditors that the IRS has a right to your interests in your current assets and any assets you acquire after we file the lien; it can affect your ability to get credit.

expected_answer_facts: The taxpayer may lose a claim to a refund or certain credits because claim periods have strict time limits.
If money is owed, penalties and interest continue until the return is filed and the balance is paid in full.

response.answer: IRS guidance says: If you don’t file, you may lose your claim to a refund or certain credits because the Internal Revenue Code sets [strict time limits](https://www.irs.gov/filing/time-you-can-claim-a-credit-or-refund) to claim those items. IRS guidance says: If you owe money, penalties and interest will continue to accrue until you file and pay in full.

Understanding your CP59 notice

Notice: CP59

Section:
Frequently asked questions > What can happen if I don’t file? (added April 17, 2025)

If you don’t file, you may lose your claim to a refund or certain credits because the Internal Revenue Code sets [strict time limits](https://www.irs.gov/filing/time-you-can-claim-a-credit-or-refund) to claim those items. If you owe money, penalties and interest will continue to accrue until you file and pay in full.
